To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
H-ferritin-mediated targeted delivery of metronomic doses of doxorubicin to 4T1 tumors prevents drug resistance and avoids cardiotoxicity.

the HFn-mediated nanometronomic chemotherapy with DOX circumvents chemoresistance and cardiotoxicity and is highly effective in treating a highly aggressive and chemoresistant 4T1 model of metastatic breast cancer.
we have developed a novel nanocage-based nanocarrier for targeted drug delivery, that is able to deliver the drug at low doses and to overcome drug resistance and drug-induced cardiotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and evaluation of a nanocaged metronomic chemotherapy, which is based on the use of HFn as a nanocarrier for the targeted and repeated delivery of DOX in the setting of an aggressive 4T1 metastatic breast cancer mouse model.
the development of novel nanomedicines for the treatment of cancer.
the development of nanocaged doxo-rubicin (DOXM) for the treatment of breast cancer, which is a leading cause of death in women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our data provide evidence that HFn- DOX administered at repeated low doses (1.24 mg/kg) strongly improves the antineoplastic potential of DOX and circumvents cardiotoxity.
the nanometronomic treatment approach with HFn-DOx, as demonstrated in this study, is an effective, non-toxic, and non-immunogenic treatment strategy for breast cancer.
our study provides a novel approach to treat advanced stage tumors with metronomic chemotherapy, which circumvents drug resistance and cardiotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the H-ferritin-mediated nanometronomic chemotherapy of breast cancer is an efficient approach to circumvent the onset of therapeutic resistance, tumor angiogenesis and cardiotoxicity, and to achieve a potent antitumoral effect with a significant increase in the overall survival of mice.
HFn-mediated targeted delivery of metronomic DOX is a safe and potent nanotherapeutic approach to treat aggressive tumors, such as the 4T1 model.

HFn-encapsulated doxorubicin, when administered at low dose (1.24 mg/kg) in a repeated manner (3 times a week) is capable of arresting the tumor progression and metastasis of 4T-1 breast cancer, while avoiding the cardiotoxicity and the development of chemoresistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nanometronomic treatment can be an effective approach for breast cancer chemotherapy, as it can circumvent the onset of chemoresistance and cardiotoxicity.

the nanocage approach to drug delivery is a promising tool for improving the therapeutic index and efficacy of chemotherapy, and that the combination of nanocaging and metronomic dosing can provide a powerful tool for improving the efficacy of chemotherapy while reducing the risk of cardiotoxicity.
nanometronomic chemotherapy with nanocaged DOX is effective in preventing the onset of therapeutic resistance in aggressive and metastatic breast cancer.
